intro:
BATTLE OF PINDUS - 3 NOV 1940

Pindus Mountains, Epirus

In your defense sector an Italian Division tries to advance on the strategic mountain pass at the town of Metsovo and threatens to cut off our supply routes and to separate our troops in Epirus and in Macedonia. Stop the attack and chase away the Italian troops from the Pindus Mountains! Our Cavalry Division will try to surround the enemy on their right flank and encircle the Italians together with your troops.

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE The unit occupying the town Vovousa, gets the chance of a Leader!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Captain, that mule has the last two boxes for Vovousa. If the path washes out again, the company up there fights with what is already in its pouches.

dialogue.speaker: Konstantinos Davakis
dialogue.text: Then stop calling it a path and put six men on it with shovels. The Julia Division is not waiting for the rain to finish.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Italian patrols have found three gaps since dawn. We can fill them, but only by taking the battalion that has not yet climbed into the line.

dialogue.speaker: Konstantinos Davakis
dialogue.text: Commander, do I send that battalion to Vovousa, or keep it below the ridge for the first real break?

choices.text: Fortify Vovousa and join every strongpoint into one line.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 10 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Hold Vovousa lightly and form a mobile mountain reserve.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance formations 15 experience and fully refuel the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: So there is no reserve. Say it plainly; the company commanders deserve to know that the next runner brings ammunition, not relief.

dialogue.speaker: Konstantinos Davakis
dialogue.text: They will know. Vovousa holds, the posts touch, and nobody invents a private withdrawal because the telephone goes quiet. Get the wire party moving.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: A light line may bend before the reserve reaches it. I want withdrawal marks on every company map, not a general instruction to use judgment.

dialogue.speaker: Konstantinos Davakis
dialogue.text: Mark them. The battalion waits under cover with loaded mules. When the Italians show us which gap matters, it goes there whole.

orders.mission: Stop the Italian advance, secure Vovousa, and keep the road toward Metsovo open.

intro:
BATTLE OF KORYTSA - 16 NOV 1940

Morava Mountains, Albania

The Italian attack could be stopped along the entire front! Now we will take the initiative and launch an offensive on the eastern flank of the front. Target of the attack is traffic point Korytsa in Albania. A victory will strengthen the morale of our troops and our nation in general.

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE The unit occupying the town Korytsa gets the chance of gain experience!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Konstantinos Davakis
dialogue.text: Vovousa held and the Italian column recoiled before it could threaten Metsovo. The cavalry is already closing on roads the enemy believed were behind him.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Italians were stopped in the Pindus, but the battalions arrived at the next assembly area by different roads and with different numbers. We won the pass; now we count its price.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I argued for a reserve in the Pindus. Your continuous line held. I have stopped calling a gap harmless simply because a battalion waits behind it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The reserve at Pindus arrived where the map had failed. Since then the men have trusted a moving company more than a perfect line drawn at headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Lieutenant Karras has brought forty-three riders out of the Pindus with both radios working. He is outside asking whether he still has a troop or merely forty-three useful replacements.

choices.text: Keep the Pindus cavalry screen as a separate detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength cavalry detachment to the core.

choices.text: Return the riders and distribute their mountain practice.
choices.hint: Give infantry 10 experience and fully refuel the core instead of adding a unit.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Karras keeps the troop. He has already found three roads the map section insists are footpaths.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Strike the troop from the return. Its riders go to the battalions as guides, and Karras reports to the route office. He will hate the desk.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The refugee carts are coming down the Korytsa road axle to axle. One driver says the Italians left the first village; the next swears they put guns in its schoolyard.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Both reports can be true. Their rear guard is moving while we argue, and the road forks twice before the city.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Athens wants Korytsa on tomorrow's front page. I want the junction before the Italians can make a second line. Those are not quite the same order.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Will you drive on the city now, or clear the lateral roads first? Choose; I will answer for the timetable.

choices.text: Give the best ammunition and transport to a direct drive on Korytsa.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry 15 experience, and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Clear the two villages and make the road safe before approaching Korytsa.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least eight strength, fully refuel and rearm it, and give reconnaissance 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: City first. Very well. I shall give the lead battalion the trucks and ask the quartermaster to perform miracles behind it.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: No miracles. Scouts stay on both forks, and a company turns back the instant a gun opens on the supply road. The rest do not stop.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: You are giving their command another day to recover. If the city hardens, nobody in Athens will remember why the villages seemed urgent.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The battalions will remember. We clear the forks, post traffic guards, and reach Korytsa with their breakfast and shells still behind them.

orders.situation: The Italian offensive has failed. Greek forces now cross into Albania toward the road junction at Korytsa.
orders.mission: Take Korytsa and the intermediate villages without allowing the advance to outrun its supply roads.

intro:
KLISURA PASS - 6 JAN 1941

Trebeshine Heights, Albania

After your victory at Korytsa we could penetrate deep into Albanian territory. However, we need the strategic important Klisura pass to consolidate our position. You will be the right one for this job. Occupy the Klisura Pass and the surrounding heights of Trebeshine mountain range!

GOAL Take all Allies VH!

NOTE The unit occupying the Klisura Pass, gets the chance of a Leader!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Korytsa fell before the Italian command could organise a second line. The advance has become a national triumph, which means the next order will assume triumph is repeatable.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Korytsa is ours, though the road behind it is crowded with damaged vehicles and newly assigned guards. The city raised morale; it did not shorten the mountains.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: You reached Korytsa before my road reports did. Headquarters has remembered the speed and quietly forgotten how exposed the lead battalion was.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The quartermaster keeps invoking your Korytsa roads whenever operations gives him an impossible timetable. I dislike admitting that he has a point.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Pindus riders are still together. Every headquarters borrows them and none remembers to return them.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The Pindus screen was dissolved, but its route tables travelled farther than the horses would have.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The snow has covered the stakes the engineers planted yesterday. A lieutenant just led his platoon in a circle and came back furious with the mountain.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: He can be furious after he finds Ballaban. The Italian reserves use the pass; their food and wounded use the villages. We cannot cut both with the guns we have.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Put the batteries on Klisura and break the lock, or split the columns through Ballaban and Suke. I need one plan before the weather closes again.

choices.text: Concentrate the artillery and break Klisura Pass first.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give artillery 15 experience, and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Take Ballaban and Suke while light columns turn the pass.
choices.hint: Give infantry and reconnaissance 10 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The village columns will hear every shell going somewhere else. Give them extra mortars, or call them screens and spare them heroic instructions.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: They are screens. Klisura receives the guns until the pass opens. Once it does, the villages lose their road and their reason to hold.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Two columns in this snow will lose contact. I want fixed reporting hours and a flare code even the replacement officers have seen.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Issue it. Ballaban and Suke fall together; then both columns turn above the pass. No race for the first flag.

orders.situation: Italian forces hold Klisura, the pass, and a chain of villages and heights controlling the winter roads.
orders.mission: Take Klisura Pass and the surrounding objectives before winter and resistance break the offensive's cohesion.

intro:
ITALIAN SPRING OFFENSIVE - 9 MAR 1941

Trebeshine Heights, Albania

In the last few weeks the Italians reinforced their army in Albania with fresh troops and we await the start of an offensive. Defend with your troops the Trebeshine Heights and if necessary recapture lost ground!

GOAL Hold after the tenth turn 10 VH, 9 VH or 8 VH for BV, V or TV!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Klisura and its pass fell with the side roads still usable. The winter offensive has reached farther than the Italians believed a Greek army could supply.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The pass is open, but some heights changed hands more than once and the supply columns learned every crater by name. We hold Klisura; spring will test whether we hold a system.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The artillery officers saw Klisura open under one concentration. Now each of them finds a single decisive lock on every map. You may have taught that lesson too well.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The men from Ballaban still trust you. They noticed that the famous pass did not receive all the guns while their road received all the wounded.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I thought the Pindus needed a reserve more than a wall. Your wall held. I have kept the reserve on this map anyway; one correct decision has not made me less cautious.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The battalion you kept back in the Pindus found the gap before headquarters did. I held one here without waiting to be told. I assumed you would ask where it was.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The wire to Height 731 has been buried twice and repaired three times. The last runner brought this telephone receiver back as proof that the fourth repair is pointless.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Keep it. In a week we may need every piece of copper somewhere else.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: German columns are entering Bulgaria. There are trains for one headquarters group: west toward Kastoria, or east toward Thessaloniki. The other route will make do with what is already there.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: You have held this front when holding mattered. Now tell me where your staff goes when the German attack begins.

choices.text: Take command in Western Macedonia and cover the mountain withdrawal.
choices.hint: Route the campaign through Lake Kastoria and Metsovo Pass.

choices.text: Take command in Central Macedonia and keep the road to Thessaloniki open.
choices.hint: Route the campaign through the retreat and evacuation at Thessaloniki.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Western Macedonia leaves us farther from the fleet and closer to encirclement. I recommend Thessaloniki.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: And I recommend we stop pretending the western corps can withdraw through a mountain road without someone there to keep it open.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Western Macedonia, then. Take the wireless truck. You will receive no second headquarters if that one is lost.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The western battalions will hear that the port mattered more. Some of them will be right to hate us for it.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: They may. Thessaloniki keeps an army connected to its allies. We go east tonight and make that connection last longer than the frontier.

RETREAT TO THESSALONIKI - 8 APR 1941

South of Doiran Lake, Central Macedonia

As expected, the Germans invaded our country in support of their unsuccessful Allies, the Italians. German armored forces, through Yugoslavia bypassing the Metaxas Line, are on their way to Thessaloniki and threaten to encircle our East Macedonia Army. I fear that we are not able to stop the Germans here. Withdraw your troops immediately to Thessaloniki and try to establish a new defense line there. Use for your non-motorized units the railway line Kilkis-Thessaloniki to escape the rapid German forces!

GOAL Retreat 22 ground units via Exit Points or hold after the eighth turn 4 VH for BV! Hold after the eighth turn 3 VH or 2 VH for V or TV!

NOTE It is advisable to delay the deployment partly until the second turn, and then to send non-motorized units immediately via train on their journey. In this mission the AI has the first turn!

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: All ten positions held through the Italian effort. The front has survived its last purely Italian battle; German columns are already crossing the Balkan map.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The spring offensive failed, though parts of the line were recovered only at the final hour. Headquarters calls it stability while ordering armies to prepare for movement north.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Kastoria battalions know why our wireless truck came west. The men outside Thessaloniki know as well. Neither group needs a staff explanation.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Thessaloniki kept us tied to the fleet and left the western corps to colder arithmetic. I defended your choice in headquarters. I did not ask the western officers to forgive it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Trebeshinë reserve is waiting beside the trucks, still under its own officers. Half the line wants its veterans; the battalion wants to remain the unit that survived together.

choices.text: Keep the mountain reserve as a separate battalion.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength mountain infantry detachment.

choices.text: Return its men and stores to the battered core.
choices.hint: Restore every core formation to at least eight strength and give infantry 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Keep their number on the board. They board the trucks as a battalion and take the rear-guard assignment together.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Remove the battalion card. Its ammunition and veterans fill the empty companies before the column moves. Nobody gets a parade for being redistributed.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Someone has painted blue arrows on the eastbound road. They are now under Greek carts, two fuel lorries, a flock of sheep, and what appears to be a municipal piano.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The piano has better road discipline than the lorries. German armoured cars are reported north of Pedino.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: If we defend every junction, the fighting units queue behind their own rear guards. If we clear the road, one German patrol can turn the queue into wreckage.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Do we build a defended corridor through Pedino and Assiros, or put every serviceable truck under the combat units and shorten the rear guard?

choices.text: Build a defended corridor through the road junctions.
choices.hint: Give infantry and anti-tank formations 10 experience and restore the core to at least eight strength with full ammunition.

choices.text: Give transport priority to the fighting formations and shorten the rear guard.
choices.hint: Fully refuel the core and give reconnaissance formations 15 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: A corridor, then. Give me closing hours for each junction. British traffic control can work with an hour; it cannot work with 'until the situation changes.'

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: I'll find the men to hold them. Do not ask those men to discover their closing hour from the backs of the last trucks.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The rear guard goes light while the guns ride. That will look sensible from the port and rather different from the final village.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I know. Combat columns move first. Broken vehicles are emptied on the spot, and nobody stops the road to save a staff car.

THESSALONIKI - EVACUATION - 9 APR 1941

Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia

Thessaloniki is not to hold - Evacuate your troops to Athens via sea immediately! The remains of the Krussia Detachment and the 19th Motorised Infantry Division try to kept clear your back as long as possible!

GOAL Retreat 9 ground units (in sea transport) via Exit Points or hold after the seventh turn 4 VH for BV! Hold after the seventh turn 3 VH or 2 VH for V or TV!

NOTE Due to the short time between the missions at HQ no new units can be recruited!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The main columns reached the exits before German armour could split the road. Thessaloniki has received an army, though the harbour cannot promise room for all of it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Enough of the road remained open to keep the retreat moving. Some rear guards arrived at the port without their guns; some guns arrived without crews.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The port officers have copied the closing-hour table from our road junctions. For once, an orderly retreat has convinced the next headquarters that order can be repeated.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: You pushed the combat columns through before the Thessaloniki road closed. The port received more veterans—and fewer men able to hold the approaches behind them.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Trebeshinë reserve is still a unit rather than a memory. It has been assigned every difficult slope since.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The reserve was dissolved into the formation, leaving no famous battalion and fewer hollow companies.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Nine berths, nine unit numbers. The hospital commandant has written names in every margin and sent the list back to me without a covering note.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: He thought the names were the note.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The first tide can take formed battalions or stretchers. If it tries to take both, officers will settle the question at the gangway and the ships will sail half-loaded.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Who boards first: the units that can fight again, or the wounded and broken formations that cannot hold the quay?

choices.text: Give the first berths to formed combat units.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Load the hospital and broken units first; the veterans hold the quay.
choices.hint: Spend 75 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The veterans get the first ship because they can survive waiting for the second. That is a soldier's joke, Commander, and I advise you not to repeat it on the quay.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: First tide to formed units. I will put the second sailing time in writing and hand it to the rear-guard commanders myself.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The brigade commanders will say we embarked men who cannot be used while leaving behind men who can. They will be correct.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: And the hospital will move before dark. Tell the veterans the truth: they are buying those berths, and no ship is promised after the second tide.

LAKE KASTORIA - 15 APR 1941

Lake Kastoria, West Macedonia

As expected, the Germans invaded our country in support of their unsuccessful Allies, the Italians. Our East Macedonia Army capitulated already, our forces in Western Macedonia are destroyed and the Germans are close to Kozani. Thus our main forces in Albania threatens to cut off! We have no other choice but to immediate withdrawal from Albania. Advance with your troops immediately to Lake Kastoria and save our line of retreat!

GOAL Retreat 6 ground units via Exit Point or hold after the ninth turn 4 VH for BV! Hold after the ninth turn 3 VH or 2 VH for V or TV!

dialogue.text: The major keeps his battalion and the next ridge. He understands that surviving intact has earned him the first difficult job.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Send his veterans to the weakest battalions before dawn. The reserve name ends here; its experience does not.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Dendrochori has three headquarters in it and room for none. Their clerks keep asking which road is reserved for them. I keep pointing south.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: German patrols are feeling for the lake road. Hold the northern posts too long and they miss the exit; pull them now and the patrols reach the column.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Fix a closing hour and defend Dendrochori until it, or shorten the front before the road becomes a trap.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Give me the hour in ink. A captain under attack will always hear 'hold until relieved,' even when nobody said it.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Write it on every order. Dendrochori holds until then and not a minute for honour. The western armies need the road more than another monument.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: We will be accused of opening the approach before the column was clear.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Then let the accusation travel on foot. The exposed companies move before dawn; the last trucks lift the roadblocks behind them.

intro:
METSOVO PASS - 19 APR 1941

South of Grevena, West Macedonia

After your breakthrough at Lake Kastoria we could not hold open the gap for long time and only a few troops could escaped. You have now the Germans before and behind! A German SS unit, passed Lake Kastoria before, is already on their way to Metsovo pass and there is now the opportunity to attack this force from behind! Prevent the blockade of the Metsovo pass and allow further comrades to escape!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE Due to the short time between the missions at HQ no new units can be recruited!

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The Kastoria road remained usable until the main body passed. German patrols reached the exit after the last organised rear guard had already turned south.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The required units came through, though the rear guard crossed in fragments. Metsovo will receive the survivors and the arguments about who stayed too long.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Dendrochori closed on the minute you ordered, although two captains tried to turn the delay into a last stand. I trust your hours now more than their enthusiasm.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: You shortened the Kastoria position before the road closed. More units reached Metsovo; the troops left on the northern shore had fewer hours bought for them.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Trebeshinë reserve remained intact and became the unit everyone called when a road had only one more hour.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: No separate reserve survived the reorganisation, but fewer western battalions arrived at Metsovo as names without strength.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Three roadblocks ahead. The first has an antitank gun, the second has felled trees, and the third is known only because every refugee points at it without stopping.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: One heavy group can batter through in order. Light parties can climb around and take the intersections, but their guns will remain down here with us.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: I require a road by nightfall. Which risk do you want entered in the signal: a slow concentration, or light groups beyond artillery support?

choices.text: Form one heavy group and smash through the roadblocks in sequence.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry and artillery 15 experience, and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Send light groups over the ridges to seize the intersections behind the roadblocks.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance 20 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Concentration means the third roadblock hears us coming for hours.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: It also means our infantry hears its own guns. Put the engineers in front, displace the batteries after each position, and keep the recovery trucks off the centre of the road.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: If a light group is pinned beyond the ridge, there is no respectable way to rescue it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Then give them mortars, wire cutters, and permission to leave any hill that is not a road. They are opening the pass, not conquering the clouds.

Levadia, Central Greece

The Empire forces have set up a defensive position at Thermopylae to cover the evacuation of their main forces. Hasten to meet them and take over their positions, so that these forces also have a chance to escape across the sea!

GOAL Hold after the tenth turn 7 VH, 6 VH or 4 VH for BV, V or TV!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text: You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The required formations embarked before the harbour became untenable. The Royal Navy reports an orderly lift; the city behind the last ship reports something less tidy.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Enough troops came out of Thessaloniki to form another line. Equipment and men remain behind in proportions no communiqué will explain.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The pass opened before the German blocking force could settle. The western columns are already feeding into the wider withdrawal toward Thermopylae.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Metsovo is open, but some columns waited within sound of the fighting until the last roadblock fell. They will reach Thermopylae tired and still formed.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The battalions from the first tide are formed and ready. The hospital has also arrived. Its missing beds are a rather exact comment on our loading order.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The hospital sailed on the first tide from Thessaloniki. The veterans paid for those berths with hours on the quay, and neither group has forgotten.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The heavy group left a clear pass and a remarkable pile of broken vehicles. Recovery still curses the method; operations has already copied it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Those light groups found a route no staff map admitted existed. Since then every staff map has acquired an imaginary mountain path. I keep asking who is meant to find it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: We went west for the battalions most likely to be cut off. The Thessaloniki columns have joined us now. Their empty places are the part of your order nobody put in the signal.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The port kept this formation connected to the fleet. Western officers have joined us at Thermopylae and speak to me only about ammunition. I am grateful for their discipline and not fooled by it.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: These times belong to ships at Rafina and trains south of Thebes. We do not know the passengers, but every hour we lose here arrives late for them.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Ten villages, ten requests for a battalion. Brallos, Amfiklia, and Levadia can cover the roads with three. The other seven requests come with mayors attached.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Do we make the enemy deploy across the whole line, or put the guns on those three hinges and keep the tractors facing south?

choices.text: Distribute the guns and hold the broad delaying line.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience, restore the core to at least eight strength, and fully rearm it.

choices.text: Concentrate on Brallos, Amfiklia, and Levadia and keep transport ready.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least eight strength, fully refuel and rearm it, and give reconnaissance 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The guns will be in penny packets. When one is lost, nobody will admit the line required it to stand alone.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The broad line buys delay in small amounts. Issue withdrawal times by sector. I want no new Leonidas deciding that his village is history's chosen pass.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The outer villages will think we abandoned them before the battle.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Send runners before the Germans cut the telephones. Three hinges get the guns; the outer posts get trucks and an order they can actually obey.

CRETE - INVASION - 20 MAY 1941

Chania, Crete

The crazy Germans actually try to conquer Crete from the air! Thwart this venture and destroy the German airborne troops!

Hold after the twelfth turn 6 VH, 5 VH or 4 VH for BV, V or TV!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn! Last chance to buy a tank for the next six scenarios! ;)

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The line held through every scheduled hour. German columns reached the southern roads after the evacuation timetable had already moved beyond them.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The required part of the line survived, though several positions closed earlier than planned. The withdrawal continues because enough roads remained contested.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Thermopylae line broke before the timetable was complete. Crete is not a reward for survival; it is simply the next place where the remaining units can still stand.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The broad line made the Germans deploy again and again. It bought the fleet its hours. I have the village casualty returns beside the sailing table if anyone wants the complete calculation.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Brallos, Amfiklia, Levadia—and tractors still attached to the guns. Some officers called your line thin. Those officers reached the ships with it.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The Thermopylae anti-aircraft section has reached Crete with three guns and ammunition for rather more. The gunners want their unit back. Every battalion wants the belts.

choices.text: Keep the anti-aircraft machine-gun section intact.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength AAMG detachment.

choices.text: Distribute the gunners and ammunition through the core.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength and fully rearm it.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Return the three guns to them. They already know how to fire while the road behind them is disappearing.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Distribute the belts and post the gunners as instructors. There will be no section on the chart, only fewer men looking upward for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The first parachutes looked like scraps of cloud. Now the schoolyard is a dressing station, and the same villagers carry ammunition uphill and wounded men down.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Hill 107 sees Maleme. If the Germans hold it, tomorrow's troops arrive in aircraft instead of under silk.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: And if every reserve goes to the hill, the docks and the road through Aghya belong to whoever lands second.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Do we commit now to Hill 107, or keep the reserve moving between Aghya and the docks until the landings show their weight?

choices.text: Commit the reserve to Hill 107 and the airfield approaches.
choices.hint: Give anti-aircraft and anti-tank formations 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Keep a mobile reserve between Aghya and the docks.
choices.hint: Restore the core to at least nine strength, fully refuel and rearm it, and give reconnaissance 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Then give the villages rifles and a signal plan. You are taking away the one formed unit that could answer them.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The reserve moves at once. Hill 107 is not another summit; it decides whether the enemy can turn an airborne raid into an airfield.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: By the time the picture is clear, Maleme may already have a runway full of transports.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The reserve carries stretchers with its ammunition and moves when a landing begins to organise. I can find guides for the roads; I cannot replace the battalion if the hill swallows it.

CRETE - EVACUATION - 28 MAY 1941

Sphakia, Crete

The withdrawal from Crete, the evacuation to Egypt was ordered - the island is not to hold! Move to the south coast of the island and board the waiting vessels!

GOAL Retreat 12 ground units (in sea transport) via Exit Points!

NOTE Due to the short time between the missions at HQ no new units can be recruited!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The airborne lodgement failed to become a secure bridgehead. Crete still stands, and the formation can move directly to the rebuilding army in Egypt.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Enough of western Crete held to keep the defence coherent, but the airfields are becoming roads for the enemy. The argument has changed from reinforcement to evacuation.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Cretan positions collapsed into separate fights. Ships and mountain tracks are now the only plan shared by the survivors.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: You committed early to Hill 107. Every later report measures the defence from that height, including the roads the reserve could no longer cover.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: You kept the Cretan reserve moving between the docks and Aghya. More roads stayed open, though every officer on Hill 107 remembers the companies he did not receive.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The Thermopylae anti-aircraft section remained together. On Crete it finally received more aircraft than anyone had wanted it to see.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The Thermopylae section was broken up, but its observers taught every battalion to look upward before the first transport appeared.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The naval signal promises one night and two beaches. It does not promise that a ship which leaves full will come back.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The field hospital reaches Sougia tomorrow afternoon if the road holds. I have stopped telling the wounded what time the fleet sails.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The formed column can make tonight's loading. Wait for the hospital and we ask the rear guard to fight through another daylight.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Commander: meet the fleet with the units already formed, or hold Sougia and bring down everyone we can still move?

choices.text: Form one fast column and meet the fleet's loading schedule.
choices.hint: Fully refuel and rearm the core and give transport and reconnaissance 15 experience.

choices.text: Hold Sougia and bring the hospital and stragglers down first.
choices.hint: Spend 75 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Give me the names of the rear guard before you give Hale the loading numbers. I will not let the missing become 'stragglers' in the first report.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Each unit gets a beach and a final time. The column moves now. Anyone who misses his place does not stop the one behind him.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: One more daylight may cost the rear guard and the ships. I cannot improve that arithmetic for you.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The hospital starts now. The rear guard gets the true sailing time, not a comforting rumour. If the last ship turns away, they will know before we do.

Alam Naghil, south of El Alamein, Egypt

It is time to expel the Axis from Egypt! The offensive against the German-Italian positions at El Alamein has begun. Your troops have the task to attack the enemy positions east of Ruweisat Ridge and - if possible - to capture. The main attack will take place in the North and - in case of success - force the entire German-Italian front to retreat!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE A fighter squadron, trained and equipped by our British Allies, is subject to your command. Congratulations!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The line held through every scheduled hour. German columns reached the southern roads after the evacuation timetable had already moved beyond them.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The required part of the line survived, though several positions closed earlier than planned. The withdrawal continues because enough roads remained contested.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Thermopylae line broke before the timetable was complete. Crete is not a reward for survival; it is simply the next place where the remaining units can still stand.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The required formations reached the exits on the first schedule. The fleet carried away a fighting body rather than disconnected survivors.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Twelve formations came out, some through Sougia and some from beaches never printed on the orders. The missing are now lists carried by three different headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Too few formations reached the exits. The survivors in Egypt will be called a reconstituted army because no government can afford the honest word fragments.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The broad line made the Germans deploy again and again. It bought the fleet its hours. I have the village casualty returns beside the sailing table if anyone wants the complete calculation.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Brallos, Amfiklia, Levadia—and tractors still attached to the guns. Some officers called your line thin. Those officers reached the ships with it.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The units with loading numbers are formed in Egypt. Those beyond the final number heard the screws turn offshore. I signed both lists.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: You held Sougia for the hospital and the scattered columns. Egypt received more wounded men—and a rear guard reduced by the time it bought them.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Six carriers came out through Sougia on the first schedule. Their officer has polished the evacuation numbers off the doors and would like to know whether that makes them a section again.

choices.text: Keep the Crete carrier section as a separate detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength Universal Carrier reconnaissance detachment.

choices.text: Distribute the vehicles, fuel, and veterans through the core.
choices.hint: Give every formation 5 experience and fully refuel the core.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: It does. Keep the drivers and vehicles together; they have already learned what a column needs when the road ends at the sea.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: No separate section. Each battalion gets drivers and a carrier if one survives inspection. The officer may keep one door with the number on it.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The barrage begins at 21:40. For once, Major Laskaris, there are more British guns behind your men than German guns in front of them.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: And British lorries, fuel, wireless sets, and aircraft. I have written the list myself often enough to understand the debt.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: This came through three couriers from Thessaly. Villages are obeying EAM committees because those committees stayed when the state left. They ask which Greece this army intends to liberate.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The men ask a shorter question. If the answer splits the brigade, who tells the half that wakes tomorrow without its officers?

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Before the barrage, I need the order for what follows it. Remain with the recognised government and Allied command, or leave the exile army and make for ELAS. I will not disguise either as the easy duty.

choices.text: Remain with the Greek government and the Hellenic Army.
choices.hint: Route the campaign through the government army, Italy, Athens, and the anti-DSE operations.

choices.text: Leave the exile army and join EAM-ELAS inside Greece.
choices.hint: Route the campaign through ELAS, the December fighting, and the Democratic Army.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: I will not call you a coward for refusing a war with Britain. But do not call obedience neutral when British weapons decide which Greeks return with authority.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I won't. We keep the formation, the oath, and the means to fight Germany. In return, we accept a chain of command we may later have to resist without breaking it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Then tell the men exactly that. No speeches about unity. We are preserving an army and inheriting its creditors.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: London will call it desertion, Cairo may call it mutiny, and Greek guards may fire before either ministry chooses a word. I thought you should hear that from me.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I signed the movement order. I will not let the formation leave as a collection of fugitives. Records, routes, families—give me the night to make a command out of the break.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The couriers sail as soon as we reach the coast. ELAS will welcome trained officers and watch them closely. We go home without pretending we arrive innocent of exile politics.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Ruweisat and Deir el Mreir fell before the Axis line could adjust to the main offensive. The Greek contingent has earned the dangerous privilege of being useful to every political plan for liberation.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The assigned objectives were taken and the Axis position is withdrawing. The formation has proved it can fight again; now every claimant to Greece asks whom that force obeys.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: You kept the formation under government command when leaving might have felt cleaner. I defended that as duty. The wire around these Greek barracks is where the defence becomes difficult.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Cairo's orders now call us deserters. The fishing captain is ready for the road home. Hale's sentries, unfortunately, are ready as well.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The Crete carriers remained together and became the formation's unofficial proof that retreat could still preserve skill.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Crete transport pool vanished into the core. Its veterans are everywhere and therefore receive credit nowhere.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The rifles are stacked inside the wire, but nobody has surrendered the keys to the armoury. Half the sentries wear no belts. The other half have loaded magazines hidden in their tunics.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The Eastern Harbour, wireless station, and arsenals must be under control before dark. If the committees talk to one another tonight, tomorrow we clear every barracks separately.

dialogue.speaker: Georgios Papandreou
dialogue.text: You remained with the government because an army requires lawful command. I will not prove that claim by treating every conscript behind this wire as an enemy.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Some followed a committee. Some followed their company because that was where breakfast was. Arrest the first group as if it were the second and by morning there will be only one group.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Do we take the command points in one stroke, or open unit-by-unit surrender corridors and accept the delay?

choices.text: Strike first at the harbour, arsenals, and wireless stations.
choices.hint: Give infantry and anti-tank formations 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Offer unit-by-unit surrender, protect the hospital, and isolate only those who keep fighting.
choices.hint: Spend 100 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Then the first shot had better be at a lock, not a window. These are Greek barracks, even when the wrong men hold the keys.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Harbour, wireless, arsenals—in that order. Once they are isolated, each unit gets one instruction to stand down. No freelance reprisals.

dialogue.speaker: Georgios Papandreou
dialogue.text: Negotiation will be called weakness in Cairo and betrayal in some of my own ministries. I accept that. I do not accept terms which leave armed committees in command.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The terms will name an hour, a collection point, and what happens to the men afterward. If we ask them to trust the government, the government must sign its name.

intro:
FOGLIA RIVER - 2 SEP 1944

South of Foglia River , Italy

Welcome in Italy! The attack on the Gothic Line is under way! However, the German resistance is stronger than expected and parts of the British 8th Army must already be taken out of the front due to high losses and exhaustion. Your troops will replace these units. Perform a frontal assault against the German defense at the Foglia River and show our Allies friends to what Greeks are able!

GOAL Hold after the ninth turn 12 VH, 11 VH or 9 VH for BV, V or TV!

NOTE The unit occupying the town Morciano Di Romagna gets full replacements!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The rebel-held nodes were secured before the mutiny could coordinate another response. Government authority has been restored—and thousands of Greek servicemen now wait behind guarded wire.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The mutiny has been suppressed, but surrender, arrest, and political reprisal are already being written as the same event by different offices.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The harbour seizure now circulates through Allied staffs as a model operation. The report takes six pages. The prisoner compound appears in one sentence.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Two men who surrendered through our Egyptian corridor have joined the brigade. They recognised me before I recognised them. I am relieved they were willing to speak.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The brigade formed from men the government trusted after April. The Canadians know that; the Germans do not care. I prefer the German examination.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Morciano keeps the coastal road open. Tavullia and Montecchio offer a turning movement, provided your engineers do not outrun every lorry assigned to them.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The brigade has spent months being described as loyal. By tomorrow it may finally be described as useful.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Do we take our own line through the hills, or remain on the Canadian flank and make certain the guns and fuel arrive with us?

choices.text: Drive through Tavullia and Montecchio with the engineer companies.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige and give infantry 15 experience.

choices.text: Secure Morciano and the coastal road in step with the Canadians.
choices.hint: Give artillery 10 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: An independent thrust means independent trouble. If you lose the road, Canadian transport will not materialise because the Greek brigade has made a stirring advance.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Understood. Engineers lead through Tavullia; infantry follows before the demolitions settle. We take our own trouble and report our own position.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The men hoping for a spectacular return to combat will call this being kept on a leash.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Let them. The coastal axis gives them artillery, transport, and a corps plan that knows where they are. Morciano first; then the road opens north.

orders.mission: Secure the required objectives and open the approaches toward Rimini without breaking the brigade in its first campaign.

intro:
BATTLE OF RIMINI - 15 SEP 1944

South of Conca River, Italy

The Germans retreated behind the Conca River and established a new defensive line there. Break through that line, advance on Rimini and free the city!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE A bomber squadron, trained and equipped by our British Allies, is subject to your command. Congratulations!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The Foglia positions broke and the brigade reached the Rimini approaches with its battalions still coherent. The first official reports already use the word exemplary.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The required ground was secured, though several ridge positions held until the final phase. Canadian headquarters now knows the brigade can be relied upon—and directed.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The brigade reached the Foglia objectives before Allied liaison found our arrow. The men took it as proof that trust suits them better than supervision.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Supply never lost the brigade on the Foglia. Since then Allied headquarters has assumed Greek timetables will fit British priorities. Reliability collects its own debts.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: You can see Rimini's towers between the shell bursts. The airfield is to the west, the port to the east, and every Canadian staff officer has drawn our arrow on a different map.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Mine puts you on the coast. It is less imaginative and has the virtue of sharing a road with your ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The airfield turns the city. It also puts Greek battalions beyond the timetable Hale can protect. Commander?

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: We can envelop through the airfield or advance beside the coast. Which risk belongs to the brigade?

choices.text: Use engineers and reconnaissance to envelop Rimini through the airfield.
choices.hint: Give infantry and reconnaissance 15 experience and fully refuel the core.

choices.text: Keep the brigade on the coastal road and take the port sector in sequence.
choices.hint: Give artillery 15 experience, restore the core to at least eight strength, and fully rearm it.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: I object. Not because the turn is unsound—because the support plan ends where your arrow bends.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Objection recorded. Engineers take the airfield, reconnaissance turns at once, and the batteries displace before the Canadians have time to ask whose timetable won.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Very well. We stay on the recognised road. If the Germans leave the western approach open, I reserve the right to be annoyed by our good logistics.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: You may be annoyed in Rimini. Port sector first, batteries by phase line, and no battalion crosses the Canadian boundary chasing a rear guard.

intro:
BATTLE OF ATHENS - 12 DEC 1944

Athens, Greece

In Athens the Communists are gone over to armed struggle! At present, we have insufficient forces stationed in Athens, but the British have pledged to fly in the 4th Indian Division from Italy immediately. Beat back the communists and clear Athens and the surrounding areas from the rebels!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Rimini surrendered to Greek troops before the defence could withdraw in order. The brigade has a victory, a new name, and political weight none of its battalions requested.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Rimini is in Allied hands and the Greek brigade carried its share of the assault. The fighting lasted long enough to leave the city less intact than the ceremony will suggest.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The airfield turn worked. The brigade remembers making it; the politicians remember only the flag in Rimini. I suspect both memories will be useful to different men.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The coastal plan brought every battery into Rimini on schedule. It also taught Allied headquarters how easily a Greek operation could be folded into a larger one.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: ELAS studied what we did in the Egyptian barracks. They know we take wireless sets and arsenals before we ask men to surrender. I would have studied us too.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The Egyptian corridors worked because the men believed surrender would not hand them to private revenge. I argued for the same restraint here. I cannot promise the same trust.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The Rimini engineers are assembled in the yard with their tools packed. They can enter Athens as a company, or disappear into battalions which all claim to need them first.

choices.text: Keep the Rimini engineers as a separate assault detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength 1944 engineer detachment.

choices.text: Distribute the engineers and replacements through the brigade.
choices.hint: Give infantry 15 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Keep the company. In Italy they opened bunkers; here they will open barricades and, if we are careful, roads out of them.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Break up the return. Every battalion receives engineers and stores. No single unit becomes the government's favourite symbol from Rimini.

dialogue.speaker: Lieutenant-General Ronald Scobie
dialogue.text: Piraeus, the airfields, and central Athens are to be secured. ELAS is to disarm. All forces in this theatre come under my command; I will not negotiate that point street by street.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: A note came from Markou in the western districts. The hospitals are taking both uniforms, families are sleeping in basements, and neither side believes the other's white cloth.

dialogue.speaker: Lieutenant-General Ronald Scobie
dialogue.text: A humanitarian report is not an operational plan, Sergeant.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: No. It is the part of the plan which tells us what victory will look like from the pavement.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Do we accept Scobie's full fire and supply plan, or restrict heavy weapons and mark hospital and civilian corridors even if ELAS uses the pause?

choices.text: Accept Scobie's operational plan and full British supply.
choices.hint: Gain 50 prestige and restore the core to full strength, fuel, and ammunition.

choices.text: Limit heavy fire and recognise hospital and civilian corridors.
choices.hint: Spend 125 prestige, give infantry and reconnaissance 15 experience, and restore the core to at least nine strength.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Then put British approval on the battery maps. I want the men to know whose order reaches the street when a hospital and a roadblock share a wall.

dialogue.speaker: Lieutenant-General Ronald Scobie
dialogue.text: They will know. Fire priorities are unified; local pauses require headquarters authority. End this quickly and there will be fewer streets requiring a second decision.

dialogue.speaker: Lieutenant-General Ronald Scobie
dialogue.text: You are refusing weight that could shorten the battle. If an airfield remains closed because a corridor delayed you, the responsibility is yours.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: It is. Publish the corridors to both sides and put them on every gun map. We may lose time. We will not lose the record of where we chose not to fire.

intro:
BATTLE OF KONITSA - 25 DEC 1947

South of Konitsa, Epirus

The communist rebels have attacked the city Konitsa on the Greek-Albanian border! The garrison defended the town stubbornly and until now was able to fend off all attacks. Advance on Konitsa and expel the rebels!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Athens and Piraeus were secured before the urban front could harden further. The government survives, British troops dominate the settlement, and Greek prisoners fill Greek compounds.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The government has recovered the capital, but the battle ended through exhaustion and British weight as much as consent. Varkiza will now ask paper to contain what the streets could not.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Scobie has left Greece. His unified command ended the Athens battle and left us the institutions built under it. We cannot send those home with him.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: A nurse from the Athens corridor recognised our unit badge in Konitsa. She thanked us, then asked where the men taken from her street had gone. I could answer only the first half.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The Rimini engineers remained together. Their foreign battle honour followed them into Greek streets where honour offered less protection.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Rimini's engineers were distributed through the brigade. Their experience remained military even when the government tried to turn the victory into a factional credential.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Konitsa has built barricades before the engineers arrived. If the town falls, the DSE will announce a capital before our communiqué admits there was a battle.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The gendarmerie lieutenant asking us for ammunition wore a Security Battalion badge in 1944. Headquarters calls that experience. The baker calls him by the name he used then.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: He commands no search and no evacuation. Put an army officer over him and write the order before he receives a cartridge.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The baker on the north street has six soldiers in his cellar and his family in the shop. He asked which part of the building the army intends to save.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: If we abandon the streets, we may abandon the town. If we fill them with guns, the baker gets his answer.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Anchor the defence inside Konitsa, or hold the villages and evacuation roads with mobile groups?

choices.text: Concentrate infantry and artillery inside Konitsa.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.

choices.text: Use mobile groups to hold the villages and evacuation roads outside the town.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give reconnaissance 20 experience, and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Then mark fallback streets before the first house disappears under sandbags. The outer companies need a route into town that does not end at somebody's kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Agreed. Three urban sectors, one reserve, batteries tied to withdrawal routes. Konitsa holds from the inside.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: A mobile belt gives the DSE a chance to get between us and the town. I want no patrol out of wireless range.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: They will carry guides and evacuation parties. We hold the approaches, move families off the gun roads, and keep one company where the town can see it.

intro:
BATTLE OF VITSI - 9 SEP 1948

South of Lake Kastoria, West Macedonia

Our last operation in the Grammos mountains was a bust! Most rebels escaped in the Vitsi region. Our job is now to prevent a renewed Redoubt in the Vitsi mountains and to destroy the escaped enemy forces. We plan a coordinated attack from the south and east to encircle the rebels. Your troops will lead the attack from the south and clean the area around the Lake Kastoria!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE The unit occupying the town Dendrochori gets full replacements!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Konitsa held and the DSE assault broke before a rival capital could be proclaimed there. The government has won a political fact through a military defence.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The town remains under government control, though the surrounding villages changed hands and families crossed the lines in both directions.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Konitsa held from its streets. Headquarters now draws an anchor symbol over every threatened town. The civilians who lived under our batteries use a less elegant mark.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The mobile belt kept most of the fighting outside Konitsa. Staff college has copied the arrows and omitted the refugee columns. I kept the original map.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The Konitsa patrols have arrived with their guides, radios, and most of their fuel. The line battalions have arrived with requests for all three.

choices.text: Keep the Konitsa scouts as a separate reconnaissance troop.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength reconnaissance cavalry detachment.

choices.text: Distribute the patrols' veterans and fuel through the core.
choices.hint: Give infantry 10 experience and fully refuel the core.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Keep the troop. A guide who knows his sergeant reports more than a guide passed from headquarters to headquarters.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Dissolve it. Guides to battalion staffs, vehicles to the worn companies, fuel to the main column. The map keeps no special colour for sentiment.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The intelligence annex marks a shepherd's path in red. The shepherd who drew it has already moved his family twice, and now three captains want him as their guide.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Four towns give us objectives the government can name. The paths between them give the DSE everything it needs to leave before those names change hands.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Take the towns first and we show control. Close the routes first and the towns have time to prepare—and to learn which villagers spoke to us.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Where does the main weight go: Kastoria and Dendrochori, or the smaller routes through Korisos and Dispilio?

choices.text: Mass the guns and take Kastoria and Dendrochori first.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Send reconnaissance groups through Korisos and Dispilio before the main assault.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance 20 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The red paths stay open, then. Do not call the guides cowards when they vanish; we have painted targets on their houses by listening to them.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The guns go on the towns. Once they fall, columns turn outward without waiting for ceremony in the squares.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: Small groups in those villages can become occupation parties before they notice. Searches require officers, and guides are not to be paraded through the streets.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: I'll brief them myself. Korisos and Dispilio first; the main force moves when the paths stop carrying DSE supplies.

intro:
OPERATION TORCH - 24 AUG 1949

East of Mt Grammos, Pindus Mountains

We are on the verge of winning the war! The defeated rebels have been entrenched in the mountains at the Albania border and the General Staff has ordered a last major operation in order to complete our victory. The Americans have supplied us with modern dive bomber and they should help to destroy the strong fortifications. Chase off the remaining communist troops from their fortifications in the Grammos mountains!

GOAL Capture all VH!

briliant.text:
The final operation has ended in military success. The organised DSE positions in the area have been broken, but Greece's political settlement and the fate of the defeated remain beyond this battlefield.

Campaign complete.

victory.text:
The final operation has ended in military success. The organised DSE positions in the area have been broken, but Greece's political settlement and the fate of the defeated remain beyond this battlefield.

Campaign complete.

tactical.text:
The final operation has ended in military success. The organised DSE positions in the area have been broken, but Greece's political settlement and the fate of the defeated remain beyond this battlefield.

Campaign complete.

lose.text:
The final operation has failed to achieve its objectives. The civil war and its human reckoning continue beyond this battlefield.

Campaign complete.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The Vitsi objectives fell before the DSE could transfer its main body. The government now speaks of a final campaign as if one successful sector had already designed it.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The zone was broken, but detachments escaped toward the higher massifs. We hold the towns; the final operation will be fought against what left them.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The communiqué named the Vitsi towns before the dust settled. DSE detachments kept moving beyond them without waiting to be named. We have both reports this time.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Closing the Vitsi routes trapped more detachments and brought more night searches. The villages remember which achievement arrived at their doors.

dialogue.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
dialogue.text: The Konitsa scouts remained a formation and entered Vitsi already knowing which tracks a conventional map ignores.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The Konitsa patrols disappeared into the line units. Their knowledge spread, though no separate troop remained to challenge a bad headquarters map.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Hale wrote last month. British matériel has become American matériel, and every crate still arrives with a policy attached. He called that continuity. I think he meant it as an apology.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Markou sent the names of three families who crossed our Athens corridors. She also sent the names of two men later taken from their homes. She did not add a conclusion for us.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: We possess the superiority we lacked in every earlier year: men, aircraft, guns, and an open supply line. I intend to use it once and finish this.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Prisoner leaflets are already blowing back across our positions. They promise fair treatment. The local police have added names in pencil beside the promise.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Then remove the pencils and discipline the police. Do not confuse misconduct with an argument for leaving the DSE an army.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The operational question remains. Seal every exit and destroy the formations, or leave controlled corridors for surrender and assign troops to protect them from both sides.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Commander, this is the last plan we write together. Which order can your formations carry without becoming something else?

choices.text: Close the ring and commit every gun to destroying organised resistance.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition.

choices.text: Publish surrender guarantees and keep controlled corridors open.
choices.hint: Spend 150 prestige and restore the core to full strength with full fuel and ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Close the ring, then. Some men across it will hear artillery and decide the border is kinder than surrender. We should at least know why they ran.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Air and artillery deny movement; ground forces close by phase. No secondary missions, no local bargains, no gaps left for another season of war.

dialogue.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
dialogue.text: Corridors consume combat strength and offer the enemy another route to deceive us. I accept them because you will command them, not because I trust the slogans on the leaflets.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Terms go by radio and leaflet. Units on the corridors answer to military law; prisoners are registered before local authorities touch them. Manesis, choose the sergeants.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: I already have. They are the ones least eager for the job.
