epilogues.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
epilogues.text: The operations room is empty except for the surrender map and two locked cabinets of names. Papagos has announced the end of organised resistance. We did not fight Britain in Athens, and the larger war we feared never came. That does not open the prisons or bring the exiles home. I can defend why we obeyed. I can no longer pretend obedience settled the account.

epilogues.speaker: Eleni Markou
epilogues.text: I found three families from the Athens corridors in a village below Grammos. They remembered your maps. One of their sons was in the prison column we passed an hour later. The army survived, Britain was never made our enemy, and the civil war is ending. If the government calls everything that follows security, those saved families will know exactly what the word conceals.

epilogues.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
epilogues.text: The last corridor delivered fighters without rifles, wounded men on doors, and two officers still arguing over rank. That is a better return than a ravine full of bodies. In Athens we accepted British command because the alternative looked like military ruin and perhaps a war far beyond Greece. We escaped that danger. The guards closing the camp gate remind us that escaping one danger does not make every later order honourable.

epilogues.speaker: Petros Manesis
epilogues.text: The sergeants from the surrender posts have brought me their registers. No blanks, no men handed over without a name. We kept corridors in Athens and opened them again here. That saved lives. It did not decide what the police will do with those lives tomorrow. You kept faith with the soldiers under your order, Commander. The country will now test whether that was enough.

epilogues.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
epilogues.text: There is a red pencil gap on every copy of the encirclement map. Formations escaped through it, and the casualty telephone has not stopped. We once accepted British command because we feared defeat, isolation, and a wider war no Greek cabinet could control. We did avoid that war. We did not avoid this one, and obedience has offered no refuge from the result.

epilogues.speaker: Eleni Markou
epilogues.text: The ring opened under attack and the villages are filling with search parties. I still meet people who lived because your Athens corridors stayed on the gun maps. They ask whether the same army has forgotten how to distinguish a road from a trap. I have no answer for them. The war continues, and restraint remembered is not restraint practised.

epilogues.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
epilogues.text: The surrender loudspeakers are still on the trucks. Few heard them before the attack failed. We preserved this army under British command and told ourselves preservation would keep later choices in Greek hands. Today Greek headquarters chose, Greek battalions paid, and the decision still escaped us. The lesser danger was real. So is everything it failed to prevent.

epilogues.speaker: Petros Manesis
epilogues.text: We brought back wounded from both sides through the corridor and lost the ground beyond it. Headquarters calls that a failure, which is fair. The men ask whether the war would be over if we had been less careful. I told them I did not know. It is the first honest answer I have given them in some time.

intro:
ESCAPE FROM EGYPT - 8 MAY 1943

Military Prison Al-Qabbari, Alexandria

The renowned hero now only a public enemy! Jailed in the military prison of Al-Qabbari you are waiting for your trial because of communist propaganda and insubordination against the Middle East High Command and the Greek government in exile. However, your friends managed to organize your escape to Greece and to provide you with a getaway car. At the airport of Alexandria a plane is ready for take off and alternatively a vessel waiting for you located in the port of Al Muaddiyah. Reach one of these points without to be caught at the control points of the Brits! Friends on the Greek freighters SS Dimitrios Inglessis and SS Thrace monitor the airport and the port for you!

GOAL Retreat your MSU via Exit Point!

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Ruweisat and Deir el Mreir fell before the Axis line could adjust to the main offensive. The Greek contingent has earned the dangerous privilege of being useful to every political plan for liberation.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: The assigned objectives were taken and the Axis position is withdrawing. The formation has proved it can fight again; now every claimant to Greece asks whom that force obeys.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: You kept the formation under government command when leaving might have felt cleaner. I defended that as duty. The wire around these Greek barracks is where the defence becomes difficult.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Cairo's orders now call us deserters. The fishing captain is ready for the road home. Hale's sentries, unfortunately, are ready as well.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: The Crete carriers remained together and became the formation's unofficial proof that retreat could still preserve skill.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The Crete transport pool vanished into the core. Its veterans are everywhere and therefore receive credit nowhere.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The captain leaves Al Muaddiyah when the harbour patrol changes. He has space for men or crates. Every officer who heard that sentence decided his own crate was indispensable.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I can provide movement papers for the first lorry and perhaps the second. After that, the guards will see an armed column moving without orders.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Most of those guards are Greeks. Yesterday they shared our cookhouse. Tonight one of them may be expected to stop us for the sake of a government we have just left.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Do we take the transport and weapons we will need in Greece, or leave them behind and reach the boat without making this a battle against our old barracks?

choices.text: Seize transport and weapons before breaking for the exits.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry and anti-tank formations 15 experience, and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Travel light and avoid fire on Greek or British guards unless the exit is closed.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: If a sentry blocks a crate, the crate stays. Force is for the road and only the road. I will not begin our return to Greece by inventing an enemy here.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Store parties first, drivers ready, no firing without your order. We will arrive better armed and with more men wondering whether we stole from them.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Light, then. The men will complain until they realise they can walk past a checkpoint without looking like an invading army.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: Hospital stores, personal weapons, papers. Everything else remains on the inventory. Discipline must carry what the lorries do not.

East of Kalabaka, Thessaly

Welcome to Greece, Commander! Experienced leaders like you we are needed urgently. The 13th ELAS Division is now under your command and your first task is a punishment operation against the traitorous EDES Bandits be making common cause with the Germans! Currently, the EDES control parts of the road Ioannina-Metsovo-Kalabaka. You will attack the EDES around Kalabaka and bring the area back under our control!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE If you do not like the composition of your new Core, you can sell units and acquire new ones with same experience. However, the increased 35% chance for a leader get lost. New units start with a chance of 10%!

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The detachment cleared the exits before the cordon closed. It will reach Greece with trained cadres and a story every side will retell differently.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Enough of the detachment escaped to remain a formation. The men left behind will face courts, camps, or a second attempt without us.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The rifles from Egypt made us a detachment before ELAS had decided whether to trust us. The Greek guards we passed tell the story differently. Both versions have followed you into these mountains.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: No funeral closed the quiet channel I kept to Cairo. The government still calls us deserters, but families and messages have crossed that channel. Your restraint bought more than a clean departure.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The mounted party from Egypt has reached these passes with the same officers and nearly the same horses. ELAS can use it as a troop, or use every rider as a courier by tomorrow.

choices.text: Keep the mounted group as an ELAS reconnaissance detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength ELAS cavalry detachment.

choices.text: Distribute the riders, fuel, and veterans through the core.
choices.hint: Give infantry 10 experience and fully refuel the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Keep them together. They crossed enough frontiers to deserve one commander who knows all their names.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Split the troop. The valleys need couriers, guides, and men who have seen an army move farther than the next village.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: EDES has put British rifles in the passes and a Greek flag over the depot. They expect those two facts to settle who commands here.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Their headquarters and stores are legitimate targets. Their village companies are another matter. Turn every EDES man into a hunted enemy and the occupation receives a civil war for free.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: Our new commander has come from Cairo. Let us hear whether Cairo taught caution or merely dressed it better.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Cairo taught us what happens when Greeks stack rifles under somebody else's guard. It did not teach us to leave an armed rival on our road.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Do we disarm EDES throughout the area, or strike its command posts and publish terms for rank-and-file units that stand aside?

choices.text: Disarm every EDES formation in the area.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Strike the headquarters and stores, but offer neutrality and amnesty to ordinary fighters.
choices.hint: Spend 75 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel and rearm it.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Complete disarmament will not remain a tidy operation. Name holding areas now, and forbid the word 'traitor' in arrest lists unless someone can attach an act to it.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: Fine. Rifles collected, officers separated, village companies sent home without weapons. Nobody changes his unit's name and keeps the depot.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: Amnesty leaves men, couriers, and grudges in place. When they return with British ammunition, I will remind you whose signature they carried away.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: You may. The terms name units, hours, and collection points. Headquarters that refuse them are attacked; men who accept them leave unarmed.

South of Korifasi, Peloponnese

You will carry out a strike against the German occupation forces on the western Peloponnese. Target of your attack is the 41st Fortress Division and the neutralization of the coastal artillery near Marathopoli. The Germans have some battle-hardened units in this area, so be careful!

GOAL Capture all VH!

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: Kalabaka and the surrounding posts fell before EDES could concentrate. ELAS controls the area, and the occupation has gained another Greek quarrel to exploit.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: The objectives are under ELAS control, though armed groups escaped the cordon. The military result is clear; its place inside the resistance is not.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: The Kalabaka passes are ours. So are the grudges carried off by men who surrendered their rifles. I still prefer an enemy without a rifle.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Some EDES men used the Kalabaka terms to go home. Others preserved their network for the next quarrel. You knew that risk and signed anyway; I have not forgotten either part.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The escape riders remained together and learned Greece one courier path at a time.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The mounted group was broken up, but its couriers tied distant ELAS units together more effectively than one cavalry troop could have.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: Those coastal guns have shelled villages and shipping for years. Take them intact and one partisan division owns more artillery than three mountain headquarters can promise.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: The guns are fixed. The German column is not. Close Kanalos and Lefki first, and the batteries can fire only while we empty the villages under them.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Evacuation has begun, but one settlement refuses to move until it sees our roadblocks. They have heard too many promises delivered after the shooting.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: Which do you want first, Commander—the guns before their crews destroy them, or the roads before the column escapes?

choices.text: Strike the coastal batteries and communications before the column reacts.
choices.hint: Give artillery and reconnaissance 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Seal Kanalos and Lefki, evacuate the villages, then destroy the trapped column.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry 15 experience, and restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Then accept that the road force may get out. Assault parties carry demolition tools; a gun we cannot turn must not be left for the next village.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: They move tonight, before the roadblocks advertise us. I want the breechblocks, not photographs beside captured barrels.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: By the time the villages are empty, the gun crews may have orders to blow everything. That is the price you are choosing.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Kanalos and Lefki close after the civilians pass. Then the column has roads on the map and none under its wheels.

intro:
BATTLE OF ATHENS - 12 DEC 1944

Athens, Greece

After the withdrawal of the Germans from Greece, the royalists have returned to our country and think they can - with the help of the disgusting Brits - rob the fruits of our liberation struggle! They also not shy away from massacre peaceful protesters to keep themselves in power. Once again it's time to take up arms and to chase these parasites out of our country!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE The British will try to fly in reinforcements, so occupy as soon as possible all airfields!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text: You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure!

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: The road force was trapped and the key positions fell before relief arrived. ELAS has gained weapons, prisoners, and responsibility for the settlements now exposed by its victory.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The objectives were taken, though part of the column escaped and some villages remained within range of the withdrawing guns. Liberation is approaching with armed Greek organisations already measuring one another.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: The Agorelitsa guns now belong to ELAS. They frighten the occupier and reassure every Greek who suspected we were preparing for a larger fight. The same barrel can do both.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: The reprisal columns found empty villages behind the Agorelitsa roadblocks. We captured fewer guns. The families who returned have not complained about the exchange.

dialogue.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
dialogue.text: You took the rifles from EDES before Britain could make more use of them. Britain has brought its own troops now. There is no pass narrow enough for this argument.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Some men who left Kalabaka under our terms are inside these districts with their families. They know we once allowed an enemy to walk away. That memory may open a door no order can.

dialogue.speaker: Georgios Siantos
dialogue.text: Scobie demands that ELAS disarm while the government keeps the formations brought from abroad. Accept that and legal politics begins at the pleasure of British guns.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: This is Major Hale on the line. The airfields and Piraeus will be opened. British reinforcements are not a bluff, and I will not insult you by presenting them as one.

dialogue.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
dialogue.text: I know your voice, Edward. I also know how quickly your lorries and guns can turn a bridgehead into a front. Do you know who lives between your phase lines?

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: A rush for the airfields might delay that weight. It will also put our best battalions where naval guns and aircraft can reach them together.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The western districts are already cutting windows into basement walls so families can pass without crossing the streets. Whatever plan we choose will arrive after the civilians have understood the battle.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: Do we strike the airfields, Piraeus, and the centre before the bridgehead hardens, or hold coherent districts and leave a channel for settlement?

choices.text: Strike the airfields, Piraeus, and central approaches before British reinforcements deploy.
choices.hint: Spend 75 prestige, give infantry and anti-aircraft formations 20 experience, and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Build a coherent district defence and keep channels for a settlement open.
choices.hint: Restore the core to full strength with full fuel and ammunition and give infantry 10 experience.

dialogue.speaker: Major Edward Hale
dialogue.text: Then we meet as enemies. I am sorry for that, Commander. It changes none of my fire orders.

dialogue.speaker: Georgios Siantos
dialogue.text: Every available battalion moves before the British line settles. We are not asking permission to remain part of Greek political life.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: I will issue the order. Keep one reserve out of the race for landmarks, or there will be no army left to exploit success.

dialogue.speaker: Georgios Siantos
dialogue.text: A defensive posture lets Papandreou call this a police action while British strength accumulates. If talks fail, the lost hours are yours.

dialogue.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
dialogue.text: They are. District sectors, local reserves, open liaison between them. We hold enough of Athens to negotiate without gambling the army on runways.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: I will send the corridor markings to both sides. Hale may ignore them. The hospitals will still know we tried before the shells arrived.

Konitsa, Epirus

Our struggle for a free Greece is now entering a decisive phase. Our political leadership has decided that we need a major city as capital for our government to gain further international validity for our fight. The choice has fallen on the city Konitsa at the Albanian border and the battle is already under way. But reinforcements are on the way to Konitsa to relieve the garrison. Fend off the attacks of the Athenian mercenary troops and bring the liberation of Konitsa to a successful end!

briefing.act: ACT IV — THE WAR IN THE MOUNTAINS

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The December assault broke the government positions before the British bridgehead was ready. Britain reversed the result and the foreign ministries ignored it. We have spent three years arguing over which fact mattered more.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: ELAS took most of its Athens objectives while British formations continued to arrive. The cadres who came out remember winning streets and losing the city. They distrust anyone who offers a simple lesson.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: I carried the ceasefire instructions through districts we no longer held. Varkiza ended the battle and left unarmed people waiting to learn whether the state would distinguish peace from surrender. Many did not wait long.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The December assault proved ELAS could contest the capital. It also proved that taking an airfield could not isolate Athens from British power outside Greece. We inherit both lessons.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The district defence brought more cadres out of Athens. It also gave Britain time to make the withdrawal unavoidable. You saved men whose next orders now come from the mountains.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Two men reached us from Thessaly. One boycotted the March election; the other voted. The same gendarmerie truck took both. Only one escaped before the ship sailed for the islands.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: A seat in that parliament would have made the terror legal, not made the Left safe.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: An empty seat spoke too. It told every organiser in Athens that the mountains were now our only argument.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The greater mistake was waiting while the factories, unions, and army still held our people. We cannot recover 1946. A government in Konitsa would at least give this struggle offices, a population, and Greek soil.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: A missed uprising is not repaired by ordering a mountain army to behave like a city. Konitsa gives the National Army walls, relief roads, and coordinates for every gun it owns.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The inhabitants are digging beside the garrison. If we call Konitsa a capital before we enter it, we have already stopped asking what they want.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Do we commit the main force to the town, or cut its roads and keep a reserve free for the relief columns?

choices.text: Commit the main force to taking Konitsa as a provisional capital.
choices.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry and artillery 20 experience, and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.

choices.text: Cut the roads, contain the garrison, and preserve a mobile reserve.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance 20 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Then publish rules for the town before the assault: no requisition without receipt, no arrest by local score-settling, and a marked hospital.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Publish them. Konitsa is taken to govern, not to raid. The reserve follows the assault once the road is open.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: A siege without possession will not make the Democratic Government more real. Do not return with captured lorries and call mobility a political result.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: I will return with an army. Cut the roads, hit relief columns, and leave the garrison the fixed battle it prepared for itself.

The battle for the Grammos mountains raged for nearly a month and the Athenian fascists send more and more mercenary troops into battle. We have no choice, we must abandon the Grammos mountains temporarily and dare the breakout! To achieve this, you will carry out a concentrated attack on the center of the enemy forces! Beat a breach in the enemy's ranks and lead our troops in Northeast direction to the Vitsi mountains!

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Konitsa has fallen to the DSE. The Provisional Government has the city it sought, but recognition and durable supply do not arrive with the same flag.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The town objectives were taken after a costly fight. Government forces are regrouping outside the area, and holding Konitsa may demand more army than taking it did.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Konitsa held against the DSE and the attempt at a provisional capital failed. The political need for territory remains, now joined by the military evidence of its cost.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Konitsa taught the Party to look for territory whenever it asks whether the army has succeeded. The foreign recognition never came, but the measure remained.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The formations saved outside Konitsa are still here. So is the Party's anger at the proclamation it never issued. You now know which result each headquarters counts first.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The Konitsa mortar group carried its tubes, tables, and wounded observers out together. It can serve Grammos as a battery, or feed crews and bombs to rifle units already asking for both.

choices.text: Keep the Konitsa mortar group as a separate battery.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength 81 mm mortar unit.

choices.text: Distribute the mortar crews and ammunition through the core.
choices.hint: Give infantry 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Keep the battery. Men who carried firing tables through that retreat have earned the right to use them together.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Break it up. The rifle battalions receive observers and bombs tonight. The battery name will not keep an empty tube firing.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The army is emptying villages below Nestorio and putting families behind wire. Government staff crosses out houses; our battalions lose guides, flour, messengers, and the next recruits.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: They are not clearing ground behind us. They are removing the country a partisan army moves through. Fix us on these ridges and the pilots need only learn target numbers.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: And an army which abandons every liberated district saves Athens the trouble of admitting there is another authority in Greece.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: The western hospital has twelve mules for thirty-one stretchers. Before anyone says 'hold' or 'withdraw,' I would like to know which nineteen wounded are part of the political argument.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Commander: build the artillery front and hold Grammos, or prepare the western corridors while there is still time to move an army through them?

choices.text: Build a fixed artillery front and hold Grammos as liberated territory.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.

choices.text: Prepare three withdrawal corridors, caches, and a mobile rear guard.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance 20 experience, fully refuel and rearm the core, and set aside transport for the wounded.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Then I want local authority to withdraw a company before it disappears. A front is not strengthened by headquarters learning about a lost ridge at supper.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Local withdrawals require approval. Register the guns, deepen the shelters, and make Grammos a front the government must attack openly.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: I'll move the spare mules to the hospital. If we are staying, the wounded need a road even when the battalions do not.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The villages will hear 'corridors' and understand retreat. Once that word spreads, it moves faster than your rear guard.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Then tell them the truth before the last battalion leaves. Three routes, caches beyond each exit, closing times, and no gun defended after its crews can still move it.

orders.situation: The National Army is attacking the Grammos base area with superior artillery and air power. Three western exits offer routes out if the fixed position cannot hold.
orders.mission: Withdraw the required formations through the exits or preserve enough of the position to keep the DSE intact.

intro:
BATTLE OF VITSI - 9 SEP 1948

Lake Kastoria, West Macedonia

It has not gone unnoticed that our main forces have retreated into the Vitsi mountains. With a new offensive the enemy wants us to deathblow here. But he underestimated our remaining strength and attack with only weak forces. After we have fool him with our withdraw he is now trapped! Destroy the enemy troops - a victory is urgently needed in order to maintain the morale of our forces!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!

briliant.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

victory.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

tactical.text: You have achieved all objectives, the mission was a complete success. Good work!

lose.text:
You could not achieve your goals, the mission was a failure! You had your chance, we need commander who successfully complete orders. This was your last combat mission!

THE END!

briefing.act: ACT IV — THE WAR IN THE MOUNTAINS

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The required formations cleared the Grammos trap in order and enough positions held to disguise the movement until late. The DSE remains an army, though the massif does not remain its frontier.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The DSE escaped Grammos with losses and scattered rear guards. Vitsi receives surviving formations, hospitals, and a strategic dispute sharpened by every missing unit.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The Grammos position broke without the required force escaping in order. The survivors at Vitsi will be rebuilt under directives that call the defeat proof of insufficient resolve.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Grammos proved the DSE could defend a front. It also gave the National Army a fixed address for every new aircraft and gun. We cannot keep only the first lesson.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The Grammos corridors delivered an army instead of a martyr's list. Headquarters still speaks of abandoned ground when it means my command. You bought the formations time, not forgiveness.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The Konitsa mortar group stayed together and gave Grammos one battery whose crews understood retreat as well as fire.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Konitsa's mortar group was divided among the core. It left no famous battery, but more companies at Grammos possessed useful fire.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The Grammos rear guard came through with its local couriers still answering roll call. It can remain a partisan detachment, or vanish into formations which need its stores more than its name.

choices.text: Keep the Grammos rear guard as a partisan detachment.
choices.hint: Add an experienced seven-strength partisan unit.

choices.text: Distribute its veterans, fuel, and ammunition through the core.
choices.hint: Give every formation 5 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Keep the detachment. It knows how to leave a closing road without losing the people who make the road useful.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Distribute it. The caches go to the weak battalions; the couriers keep their routes. Survival does not require a separate flag.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The Prespa replacements include women who voted in the Free Greece elections before Athens gave women a national ballot. The roster calls three of them auxiliaries. They commanded sections at Grammos.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Then correct the roster. I need the ranks they earned and every pair of boots they brought with them.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Our comrades abroad fear that Greece could open a war none of them can contain. They praise the DSE and inspect every crate as though it carried the first shot. We must show them an army capable of a result.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Then I plan with the crates that crossed the border, not the resolutions that did. Give me food routes, guides, and two nights without aircraft; then the towns become vulnerable.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Do we mass the remaining guns against Korisos and Dispilio now, or rebuild the routes and local cells before the assault?

choices.text: Mass the surviving guns for a direct counterattack on Korisos and Dispilio.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.

choices.text: Rebuild the mountain routes and local cells before assaulting the objectives.
choices.hint: Give infantry and reconnaissance 15 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: I'll find the twenty-five pairs. I cannot find another battalion if the guns fail to move after it.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The attack begins before the National Army turns its advance into a permanent line. The people must see the DSE return, not merely hear that it survived.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Delay has become your answer to every demand for a result. If the local cells do not re-form, this operation will be remembered as preparation for nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: I accept that. Light groups go first with couriers and supply parties. We attack when the government posts discover their rear is no longer quiet.

intro:
ARIDAEA - 14 DEC 1948

East of Aridaea, West Macedonia

The liberation of Greek cities is still at the top of our priorities. Your Division will carry out an surprise attack across the Yugoslav border on Aridaea and free the city! If the resistance is broken here, the further advance on Veroea and Edessa is planned. Let's hope that you succeed and meet an unprepared enemy!

GOAL Capture all VH!

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The Vitsi objectives were recovered before government forces could consolidate. The DSE has regained a district and not the strategic balance beyond it.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: Korisos and Dispilio fell after hard fighting. The core survives, but every replacement now comes from a population already divided and exhausted.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The counterstroke failed to restore Vitsi. The next directive will demand a result at Aridaea as if urgency could replace the formations missing here.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The Vitsi counterattack put flags back in the towns. It also revived the belief that one more fixed battle can alter the political balance. That belief now has your victory behind it.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The rebuilt Vitsi routes are carrying food and couriers again. Party reports count the days without a visible victory; the battalions count meals. I know which ledger you chose.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The detachment which covered the Grammos exits has entered Vitsi under its own officers. Retreat made it surer of itself. That is useful and, in young formations, occasionally dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The men and caches from the Grammos exits are scattered through the core now. No unit inherited the honour. Several units inherited enough strength to answer roll call.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: I warned that a fixed Grammos would become a target number. It did. You held it long enough to save something, and long enough for the pilots to learn every path we used.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The formations came out of Grammos. The villages and the claim to territory did not. You saved the instrument, Commander. I am still waiting to see what political result it can produce.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The Vitsi assault group is outside, fed and overconfident. We can keep that edge for Aridaea, or take away its extra ammunition and make certain the rest of the army reaches the town fit to move.

choices.text: Give the Vitsi veterans and ammunition to the Aridaea assault group.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 15 experience and fully rearm the core.

choices.text: Distribute the Vitsi replacements and stores through the entire core.
choices.hint: Restore every core formation to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Keep the group concentrated. A success needs a point sharp enough to enter the town before doubt does.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Level the issue. I want every formation able to leave Aridaea, including the ones which do not appear in the first communiqué.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: The quarrel between Belgrade and Moscow has reached the depots. A road open last winter now depends on which capital the frontier guard thinks we obey.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The Democratic Army does not set its policy by the mood of a frontier guard.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: No. But the wounded still cross through his gate.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: Aridaea can show that the Democratic Army still takes and governs territory. After the reverses, anything less will be described as survival.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Survival is not an insult when the alternative is a town surrounded by roads we cannot close. Take the stores, take the prisoners, leave before the National Army makes our success convenient.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: The local committee has prepared offices and a prison list. The withdrawal officer has prepared fuel dumps and departure times. Both are waiting outside, and neither will look at the other.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: So decide it now. Is Aridaea a centre we hold, or an operation we finish before the counterstroke?

choices.text: Take Aridaea and organise it as a permanent DSE centre.
choices.hint: Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.

choices.text: Seize the stores and prisoners, then withdraw on a prepared schedule.
choices.hint: Give reconnaissance 20 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: Then cancel the departure schedule. I disagree, but I will not let half the force fight with one foot on the road. Site the antitank guns before the committee hangs its first notice.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: The town is taken, organised, and defended. Authority enters behind the assault; it does not arrive later to explain why the army left.

dialogue.speaker: Eleni Markou
dialogue.text: I will take the prison list. No arrest until a name has an accusation beside it. If we mean to govern, we begin there.

dialogue.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
dialogue.text: You are choosing another disappearance. Do not expect a captured storehouse to answer the political defeat of abandoning the town.

dialogue.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
dialogue.text: No. It answers the military question of whether these battalions exist next month. Loads, routes, departure hours—issue them before the first unit enters the streets.

dialogue.speaker: Petros Manesis
dialogue.text: Good. A soldier can complete an hour. He cannot complete a promise that keeps moving farther into 1949.

epilogues.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
epilogues.text: The first proclamation came off the Aridaea press while the antitank crews were still digging. For a few weeks the town answered those who said the Democratic Army could only hide. It did not reopen the Yugoslav frontier or replace the battalions already gone. In 1949 the fixed fronts broke. The proclamation travelled into exile folded inside a uniform, proof of a state announced and never secured.

epilogues.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
epilogues.text: The last Aridaea lorry cleared the road before dawn. We took stores, prisoners, and most of the assault force home. Headquarters called the empty town another failure of nerve. In 1949 the Yugoslav frontier closed and aircraft found the roads manoeuvre could no longer replace. More of the army survived because you left. It survived long enough to lose elsewhere.

epilogues.speaker: Eleni Markou
epilogues.text: The committee's prison list never left its envelope. We carried the wounded out past offices prepared for a government that did not arrive. Children had crossed north before the last formations; some learned to write home in another alphabet before their parents knew where exile would take them. The frontier closed in 1949, and the survivors went to camps, prisons, exile, or back to villages where questions were dangerous. During the occupation we built authority from almost nothing. In the civil war, we learned how quickly authority can begin demanding everything.

epilogues.speaker: Petros Manesis
epilogues.text: The departure times were still legible when the first units came back without their loads. We saved fragments of the force, not the raid. In 1949 the border closed, aircraft watched the remaining roads, and the villages had little left to give. Some men crossed out, some surrendered, and some simply removed the insignia. No final order told us which of them had completed his duty.
